gaps.why_now: The roadmap still requires perf baselines and thresholds, so the narrowest honest progress is a manifest-backed survey packet that keeps the current benchmark-command and acceptable-limit posture machine-checked without inventing numbers. Live master now ships that packet, and the shared Phase 4 tests-root summary now names the local perf-baseline survey pair alongside the validation matrix and gate-evidence note.

A dedicated Phase 4 survey gate keeps the current correctness-only posture for the shipped atomic64 and bitmap rollback gates measurable without treating that local survey route as shared CI perf approval. With the shared tests-root summary now naming this shipped local-only survey packet, the smaller same-lane follow-through is one bounded acceptable limit per shipped gate now that both local benchmark commands are approved.

The local perf-baseline packet now exact-pins the current atomic64 benchmark-command candidate `zig build phase4-runtime-atomic64-diff --build-file zigux/tests/phase4_build.zig` plus the deterministic threshold replay evidence (`runThresholdReplay(1)` checksum `3626254113632800175` with final counter `130322557735600377`; `runThresholdReplay(4)` checksum `9210681150676220922` with final counter `130322557735600376`) without pretending that the acceptable limit is already approved or that shared CI owns the route.

The bounded atomic64 replay command is now approved for local Phase 4 perf review because the dedicated survey packet already exact-pins the same replay route and deterministic evidence, while the acceptable limit remained explicitly unapproved and the shared validator-first packet stayed narrower than full perf coverage when this command promotion first landed.

The local-only atomic64 acceptable limit is now approved as a median `runThresholdReplay(4)` budget of `8192` nanoseconds across seven monotonic samples, because the dedicated survey can keep that bounded replay budget explicit, the current local probe already measured a much lower median on the attached Zig toolchain, and the change keeps bitmap thresholds plus any shared CI perf claim explicitly out of scope.

The local perf-baseline packet now exact-pins the current bitmap benchmark-command candidate `zig build phase4-bitmap-diff --build-file zigux/tests/phase4_build.zig` plus the deterministic threshold replay evidence (`runThresholdReplay(1)` checksum `5216946504564592253` with final first-set `0`, final first-zero `109`, final weight `1005`, and final nth-seven `123`; `runThresholdReplay(4)` checksum `7942141539243507472` with the same final first-set, first-zero, weight, and nth-seven packet) without pretending that the acceptable limit is already approved or that shared CI owns the route.

The bounded bitmap replay command is now approved for local Phase 4 perf review because the dedicated survey packet already exact-pins the same replay route and deterministic evidence, while the acceptable limit remains explicitly unapproved and the shared validator-first packet still stays narrower than full perf coverage.

The next honest bounded Phase 4 perf step is now the bitmap local-only acceptable limit, because the atomic64 replay has an explicit median nanosecond budget in the dedicated survey packet while the bitmap replay still only carries approved command evidence and deterministic threshold-check replay data.
